Name: Cincinnati
Description: Where Pigs Fly, Cincinnati
LabelText: What do flying pigs have to do with Cincinnati? In the 19th century, the city’s fortunes were closely tied to river commerce and pork processing plants. In 1988, when Cincinnati decided to renovate its riverfront as part of its bicentennial celebrations, the architect of the new Bicentennial Commons proposed honoring the history of “Porkopolis” by framing the park entrance with four pigs flying atop riverboat smokestacks. The idea was ridiculed at first, but Cincinnatians soon warmed up to their puzzling mascots.
